title: SCpubr
text:
Welcome to SCpubr
Welcome to the official documentation for SCpubr v3.0.0!
SCpubr provides a streamlined way of generating publication-ready plots for Single-Cell transcriptomics data. The goal is simple: create high-quality visualizations with minimal effort that can be used right away in your research articles.

title: SCpubr
text:
What’s new in v3.0.0?

34 functions organized into 6 logical categories
Colorblind-safe palettes built-in
Standardized naming across all functions
Enhanced compatibility with SeuratObject v5
Text values in heatmaps for better readability

Check the full changelog for details.

title: Installation guide
text:
Check your dependencies
To install SCpubr, use the following commands:
SCpubr relies on several packages to run its functions. You can get a full overview of which dependencies are installed and which functions are available using SCpubr::do_PackageReport():
SCpubr::do_PackageReport(extended = TRUE)
This will provide you with:

title: Installation guide
text:
The status of your dependencies (installed or missing).
The functions that can be run based on your currently installed dependencies.
Packages that require a minimum version will be marked with an exclamation mark if outdated.

title: Dataset used
text:
Throughout this manual, we use a publicly available dataset containing 10,000 human PBMCs (peripheral blood mononuclear cells) from 10x Genomics.
Below is the code to generate a Seurat object ready for plotting, including basic quality control, normalization, dimensional reduction, and clustering:

counts_path <- "path_to_count_matrix"

# Read count matrix
counts <- Seurat::Read10X(counts_path)

# Create Seurat object
sample <- Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts, project = "10K_pbmc")

# Compute percentage of mitochondrial RNA
sample <- Seurat::PercentageFeatureSet(sample, pattern = "^MT-", col.name = "percent.mt")

# Basic QC filters
mask1 <- sample$nCount_RNA >= 1000
mask2 <- sample$nFeature_RNA >= 500
mask3 <- sample$percent.mt <= 20
mask <- mask1 & mask2 & mask3
sample <- sample[, mask]

# Normalize
sample <- Seurat::SCTransform(sample)

# Dimensional reduction
sample <- Seurat::RunPCA(sample)
sample <- Seurat::RunUMAP(sample, dims = 1:30)

# Find clusters
sample <- Seurat::FindNeighbors(sample, dims = 1:30)
sample <- Seurat::FindClusters(sample, resolution = 0.2)

This object will be used as sample in all code examples throughout the book.

title: Quick start guide
text:
Your first plot
This is a 5-minute introduction to get you started with SCpubr.
library(Seurat)
library(SCpubr)

# Load your data
sample <- readRDS("your_seurat_object.rds")

# Create a dimensional reduction plot
p <- SCpubr::do_DimPlot(sample = sample)
p

title: Quick start guide
text:
Visualize gene expression

# Plot gene expression
p <- SCpubr::do_FeaturePlot(sample = sample,
                            features = "CD3D")
p

title: Quick start guide
text:
Compare groups

# Violin plot comparing groups
p <- SCpubr::do_ViolinPlot(sample = sample,
                           features = "CD3D")
p

That’s it! You’re ready to explore the rest of the functions.

title: Shared features across functions
text:
Basic parameters
Most functions in SCpubr share common parameters. Understanding these will help you navigate the package more efficiently.

title: Shared features across functions
text:
sample: Seurat object to use for plotting.

group.by: Metadata variable to group the values by.

split.by: Metadata variable to split the plots by.

features: Genes or metadata columns to plot.

assay: Assay name to pull data from.

reduction: Which dimensional reduction to use (e.g., “umap”, “pca”).

title: Shared features across functions
text:
Customization parameters


colors.use: Custom color palette (vector of named colors).

legend.position: Where to place the legend (“right”, “bottom”, “none”).

plot.title: Title for the plot.

plot.subtitle: Subtitle for the plot.

font.size: Base font size for the plot.

title: Shared features across functions
text:
Using custom colors

# Define custom colors
colors <- c("0" = "#001219",
            "1" = "#005f73",
            "2" = "#0a9396")

# Apply to any function
p <- SCpubr::do_DimPlot(sample = sample,
                        colors.use = colors)

title: Shared features across functions
text:
Colorblind-safe palettes
Set colorblind = TRUE in any function to use colorblind-safe palettes automatically:

p <- SCpubr::do_DimPlot(sample = sample,
                        colorblind = TRUE)

title: do_DimPlot() | Dimensional reduction plots
text:
Basic usage
Dimensional reduction plots are the cornerstone of single-cell visualization. They allow you to visualize cells in reduced dimensions (UMAP, tSNE, PCA) colored by any categorical variable.
p <- SCpubr::do_DimPlot(sample = sample)
p

title: do_DimPlot() | Dimensional reduction plots
text:
Label the clusters
Remove the legend and add labels directly on the clusters:

p <- SCpubr::do_DimPlot(sample = sample,
                        label = TRUE)
p

title: do_DimPlot() | Dimensional reduction plots
text:
Split by variable
Create separate plots for different groups:

p <- SCpubr::do_DimPlot(sample = sample,
                        split.by = "orig.ident")
p

title: do_DimPlot() | Dimensional reduction plots
text:
Custom colors

colors <- c("0" = "#E63946",
            "1" = "#F1FAEE",
            "2" = "#A8DADC")

p <- SCpubr::do_DimPlot(sample = sample,
                        colors.use = colors)
p

title: do_ViolinPlot() | Distribution comparison
text:
Basic usage
Violin plots show the distribution of gene expression or other continuous variables across different groups.
p <- SCpubr::do_ViolinPlot(sample = sample,
                           features = "CD3D")
p

title: do_ViolinPlot() | Distribution comparison
text:
Multiple features

p <- SCpubr::do_ViolinPlot(sample = sample,
                           features = c("CD3D", "CD8A", "CD4"))
p

title: do_ViolinPlot() | Distribution comparison
text:
Split by variable

p <- SCpubr::do_ViolinPlot(sample = sample,
                           features = "CD3D",
                           split.by = "condition")
p

title: do_BoxPlot() | Box-and-whisker plots
text:
Basic usage
Box plots provide a statistical summary of distributions across groups.
p <- SCpubr::do_BoxPlot(sample = sample,
                        features = "CD3D")
p

title: do_BeeSwarmPlot() | Individual cell distributions
text:
Basic usage
Beeswarm plots show individual cells as points, providing a detailed view of the data distribution.
p <- SCpubr::do_BeeSwarmPlot(sample = sample,
                             features = "CD3D")
p

title: do_RidgePlot() | Density ridge plots
text:
Basic usage
Ridge plots display density distributions stacked vertically for easy comparison.
p <- SCpubr::do_RidgePlot(sample = sample,
                          features = "CD3D")
p

title: do_StripPlot() | Geyser plots
text:
Basic usage
Strip plots (also known as geyser plots) show individual observations with density-based jittering.
p <- SCpubr::do_StripPlot(sample = sample,
                          features = "CD3D")
p

title: do_BarPlot() | Categorical proportions
text:
Basic usage
Bar plots visualize the proportions of categorical variables across groups.
p <- SCpubr::do_BarPlot(sample = sample,
                        group.by = "seurat_clusters",
                        split.by = "condition")
p

title: do_WafflePlot() | Pictogram proportions
text:
Basic usage
Waffle plots display proportions as a 10x10 grid of tiles, providing an intuitive visual representation.
p <- SCpubr::do_WafflePlot(sample = sample,
                           group.by = "seurat_clusters")
p

title: do_AlluvialPlot() | Flow between categories
text:
Basic usage
Alluvial plots visualize how categorical assignments change across conditions or time points.
p <- SCpubr::do_AlluvialPlot(sample = sample,
                             first_group = "seurat_clusters",
                             last_group = "cell_type")
p

title: do_FeaturePlot() | Gene expression on dimensional reduction
text:
Basic usage
Feature plots display continuous values (typically gene expression) on dimensional reduction embeddings.
p <- SCpubr::do_FeaturePlot(sample = sample,
                            features = "CD3D")
p

title: do_NebulosaPlot() | Density-based gene expression
text:
Basic usage
Nebulosa plots use kernel density estimation to provide a smoothed representation of gene expression across the dimensional reduction space.
p <- SCpubr::do_NebulosaPlot(sample = sample,
                             features = "CD3D")
p

title: do_NebulosaPlot() | Density-based gene expression
text:
Joint density
Visualize co-expression of multiple genes:

p <- SCpubr::do_NebulosaPlot(sample = sample,
                             features = c("CD3D", "CD8A"))
p

title: do_CellularStatesPlot() | Cell state transitions
text:
Basic usage
This function visualizes cellular states and transitions across conditions or time points.
p <- SCpubr::do_CellularStatesPlot(sample = sample,
                                   group.by = "seurat_clusters",
                                   split.by = "condition")
p

title: do_DotPlot() | Marker gene expression
text:
Basic usage
Dot plots show both the expression level and percentage of cells expressing a set of genes across groups.
p <- SCpubr::do_DotPlot(sample = sample,
                        features = c("CD3D", "CD8A", "CD4"))
p

title: do_ExpressionHeatmap() | Expression heatmap
text:
Basic usage
Expression heatmaps display gene expression patterns across cells or groups.
p <- SCpubr::do_ExpressionHeatmap(sample = sample,
                                  features = c("CD3D", "CD8A", "CD4"))
p

title: do_SCExpressionHeatmap() | Single-cell expression heatmap
text:
Basic usage
Single-cell expression heatmaps show expression at individual cell resolution.
p <- SCpubr::do_SCExpressionHeatmap(sample = sample,
                                    features = c("CD3D", "CD8A", "CD4"))
p

title: do_RankedExpressionHeatmap() | Expression along components
text:
Basic usage
This function displays gene expression along a dimensional reduction component or trajectory.
p <- SCpubr::do_RankedExpressionHeatmap(sample = sample,
                                        features = c("CD3D", "CD8A"),
                                        dims = 1)
p

title: do_CorrelationHeatmap() | Feature correlation matrix
text:
Basic usage
Correlation heatmaps show pairwise correlations between features.
p <- SCpubr::do_CorrelationHeatmap(sample = sample,
                                   features = c("CD3D", "CD8A", "CD4"))
p

title: do_GroupwiseDEHeatmap() | Differential expression
text:
Basic usage
This function visualizes differential expression results across groups.
p <- SCpubr::do_GroupwiseDEHeatmap(sample = sample,
                                   de_genes = de_results)
p

title: do_VolcanoPlot() | DE volcano plots
text:
Basic usage
Volcano plots display differential expression results showing both fold change and statistical significance.
p <- SCpubr::do_VolcanoPlot(de_genes = de_results)
p

title: do_EnrichmentHeatmap() | Gene set enrichment
text:
Basic usage
Enrichment heatmaps visualize gene set enrichment scores across cells or groups.
p <- SCpubr::do_EnrichmentHeatmap(sample = sample,
                                  input_gene_list = gene_sets)
p

title: do_SCEnrichmentHeatmap() | Single-cell enrichment
text:
Basic usage
Single-cell enrichment heatmaps show enrichment at individual cell resolution.
p <- SCpubr::do_SCEnrichmentHeatmap(sample = sample,
                                    input_gene_list = gene_sets)
p

title: do_RankedEnrichmentHeatmap() | Enrichment along components
text:
Basic usage
This function displays enrichment scores along a dimensional reduction component.
p <- SCpubr::do_RankedEnrichmentHeatmap(sample = sample,
                                        input_gene_list = gene_sets,
                                        dims = 1)
p

title: do_TermEnrichmentPlot() | GO/pathway term enrichment
text:
Basic usage
This function visualizes enriched GO terms or pathways from enrichment analysis results.
p <- SCpubr::do_TermEnrichmentPlot(mat = enrichment_results)
p

title: do_ActivityHeatmap() | Activity scores heatmap
text:
Basic usage
Activity heatmaps display activity scores (from tools like decoupleR) across cells or groups.
p <- SCpubr::do_ActivityHeatmap(sample = sample,
                                activities = activity_scores)
p

title: do_TFActivityHeatmap() | Transcription factor activity
text:
Basic usage
TF activity heatmaps visualize transcription factor activity scores across cells or groups.
p <- SCpubr::do_TFActivityHeatmap(sample = sample,
                                  activities = tf_activities)
p

title: do_PathwayActivityHeatmap() | Pathway activity scores
text:
Basic usage
Pathway activity heatmaps show pathway-level activity scores across cells or groups.
p <- SCpubr::do_PathwayActivityHeatmap(sample = sample,
                                       activities = pathway_activities)
p

title: do_LigandReceptorPlot() | Cell-cell communication
text:
Basic usage
This function visualizes ligand-receptor interactions between cell types using output from tools like LIANA.
p <- SCpubr::do_LigandReceptorPlot(liana_output = interactions)
p

title: do_ChordDiagramPlot() | Interaction networks
text:
Basic usage
Chord diagrams visualize relationships and flows between different groups as circular connections.
p <- SCpubr::do_ChordDiagramPlot(sample = sample,
                                 from = "cluster_A",
                                 to = "cluster_B")
p

title: do_CNVHeatmap() | Copy number variation
text:
Basic usage
CNV heatmaps display chromosomal copy number variations across cells using inferCNV output.
p <- SCpubr::do_CNVHeatmap(sample = sample,
                           infercnv_object = cnv_results)
p

title: do_LoadingsHeatmap() | PCA loadings
text:
Basic usage
Loadings heatmaps show which genes contribute most to principal components.
p <- SCpubr::do_LoadingsHeatmap(sample = sample,
                                dims = 1:5)
p

title: do_MetadataHeatmap() | Metadata overview
text:
Basic usage
Metadata heatmaps provide a comprehensive view of metadata variables across cells.
p <- SCpubr::do_MetadataHeatmap(sample = sample,
                                metadata_variables = c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA"))
p

title: do_ColorPalette() | Color palette generation
text:
Basic usage
This utility function generates color palettes for your plots.
colors <- SCpubr::do_ColorPalette(n = 10)
colors

title: do_ColorBlindCheck() | Colorblind accessibility testing
text:
Basic usage
This function helps you verify if your color palette is accessible for colorblind readers.
colors <- c("#E63946", "#F1FAEE", "#A8DADC")

p <- SCpubr::do_ColorBlindCheck(colors = colors)
p

text:
Basic usage
Get a comprehensive report of installed dependencies and available functions.
SCpubr::do_PackageReport(extended = TRUE)

title: Basic QC workflow
text:
Overview
This workflow demonstrates a basic quality control visualization pipeline.
# Load data
sample <- readRDS("seurat_object.rds")

# QC metrics
p1 <- SCpubr::do_ViolinPlot(sample = sample,
                            features = "nCount_RNA")

p2 <- SCpubr::do_ViolinPlot(sample = sample,
                            features = "nFeature_RNA")

# Combine plots
p1 | p2

title: Marker identification workflow
text:
Workflow
A complete workflow for identifying and visualizing cluster markers.
# Visualize clusters
p1 <- SCpubr::do_DimPlot(sample = sample,
                         label = TRUE)

# Show marker expression
p2 <- SCpubr::do_DotPlot(sample = sample,
                         features = markers)

# Combined view
p1 / p2

title: Cell-cell communication workflow
text:
Workflow
Analyze and visualize cell-cell communication using ligand-receptor analysis.
# Run LIANA analysis (external)
# liana_results <- liana::liana_wrap(sample)

# Visualize interactions
p <- SCpubr::do_LigandReceptorPlot(liana_output = liana_results)
p

title: Pathway enrichment workflow
text:
Workflow
Complete workflow for pathway enrichment analysis and visualization.
# Define gene sets
gene_sets <- list("T_cell" = c("CD3D", "CD8A"),
                  "B_cell" = c("CD19", "MS4A1"))

# Visualize enrichment
p <- SCpubr::do_EnrichmentHeatmap(sample = sample,
                                  input_gene_list = gene_sets)
p

title: Creating publication-ready figures
text:
Key principles
Tips and workflows for creating publication-quality figures.

title: Creating publication-ready figures
text:
Use consistent color schemes
Add meaningful titles and labels
Check colorblind accessibility
Use appropriate figure dimensions

title: Creating publication-ready figures
text:
Example workflow

# Define colors
colors <- c("0" = "#E63946",
            "1" = "#F1FAEE")

# Check colorblind safety
SCpubr::do_ColorBlindCheck(colors = colors)

# Create figure
p <- SCpubr::do_DimPlot(sample = sample,
                        colors.use = colors,
                        plot.title = "Cell Clusters")
p

title: Advanced tips and tricks
text:
Combining plots
Advanced customization techniques for power users.
Use patchwork to combine multiple SCpubr plots:
library(patchwork)

p1 <- SCpubr::do_DimPlot(sample = sample)
p2 <- SCpubr::do_FeaturePlot(sample = sample, features = "CD3D")

# Side by side
p1 | p2

# Stacked
p1 / p2

title: Advanced tips and tricks
text:
Custom themes
All SCpubr plots return ggplot2 objects, so you can further customize them:

p <- SCpubr::do_DimPlot(sample = sample)
p + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Frequently asked questions
text:
Installation
Q: Why are some functions not working?
A: SCpubr has many optional dependencies. Run SCpubr::do_PackageReport(extended = TRUE) to see which dependencies are missing.

title: Frequently asked questions
text:
Plotting
Q: How do I change colors?
A: Use the colors.use parameter in any function. See the Shared features chapter.
Q: Can I use custom color palettes?
A: Yes! You can provide a named vector of colors to colors.use or use colorblind = TRUE for automatic colorblind-safe palettes.

title: Frequently asked questions
text:
Troubleshooting
Q: My plot looks too crowded
A: Try using raster = TRUE to rasterize the plot, or adjust pt.size to make points smaller.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Common errors

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Missing dependencies
Error: “Package X is not installed”
Solution: Install the missing package or run SCpubr::do_PackageReport(extended = TRUE) to see all missing dependencies.
Memory issues
Error: “Cannot allocate vector of size…”
Solution: Use raster = TRUE to reduce memory usage, or work with a subset of your data.
Color scale issues
Error: “Insufficient values in manual scale”
Solution: Make sure your colors.use vector has names matching all categories in your data.

title: Color palette reference
text:
Built-in palettes
SCpubr includes several built-in color palettes optimized for single-cell visualization.

title: Color palette reference
text:
Colorblind-safe palettes
When you set colorblind = TRUE, SCpubr automatically selects from a collection of colorblind-safe palettes based on the number of categories in your data.

title: Color palette reference
text:
Creating custom palettes

# Generate a palette
colors <- SCpubr::do_ColorPalette(n = 10)

# Test for colorblind accessibility
SCpubr::do_ColorBlindCheck(colors = colors)
